chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever recites ten verses in a night will not be written among the heedless. And whoever recites fifty verses will be written among the remembrers. And whoever recites one hundred verses will be written among those who perform qunut. And whoever recites two hundred verses will be written among the humble. And whoever recites three hundred verses will be written among the winners. And whoever recites five hundred verses will be written among the diligent. And whoever recites one thousand verses, a kantar will be written for him. And the kantar is five thousand mithqals of gold. And the mithqal is twenty-four carats, the smallest of which is like Mount Uhud, and the largest of which is that which is between the heaven and the earth.

key_terms.قِنْطَارٌ: A kantar, a unit of weight/value for gold
key_terms.مِثْقَالًا: A mithqal, a unit of weight for gold

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for reciting different numbers of Quranic verses at night?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, this hadith establishes a graded spiritual hierarchy based on the volume of Quranic recitation, contrasting those who remain heedless with those who attain statuses like *Qantīn* (devoutly obedient) and *Khāshīʿūn* (humble). The concluding definition of the 'kantar' as five thousand mithqāls of gold, with a single mithqāl weighing as much as Mount Uhud, serves to emphasize the immense, tangible value of consistent Quranic engagement in Shia devotional practice.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hussain bin Sa’eed, from Nadr bin Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Muhammed bin Marwan, from Sa’d bin Tareef, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said:

The one who recites ten verses at a night, will not be written to be among the unaware. The one who recites fifty verses, will be written to be among the remembering. The one who recites a hundred verses, will be written to be among the performers of qunut. The one who recites two hundred verses, will be written to be among the devoted. The one who recites three hundred verses, will be written to be among the winners. The one who recites five hundred verses, will be written to be among the diligent. The one who recites a thousand verses, to him it will be written a kantar. A kantar is five thousand mithqal [1] of gold. One mithqal is twenty four carats, of which the smallest is like Mount Uhud, and of which the biggest is (like that which is) between the Heaven and earth.
